correctness.rationale: The projective degree is reconstructed independently from the type-C Weyl dimension formula: the relevant positive coroots give exactly the displayed root product, which simplifies to the factorial expression. The Euler characteristic is the number of Bruhat cells, namely the order of the Weyl quotient \(W(C_n)/(W(A_{k-1})\times W(C_{n-k}))\), equal to \(2^k\binom nk\). For fixed \(k\ge2\), the exact adjacent-\(n\) degree quotient dominates the adjacent Euler quotient; the proof reduces this to an explicit polynomial with positive coefficients after \(u=k-2\). The boundary Lagrangian recurrence proves normalized degree exceeds one for every \(k\ge3\), while the two-plane cases are settled by the exact values at \(n=2,3\). The checker independently compares the root product, factorial product, Euler count, and both ratio identities.

value.rationale: Symplectic Grassmannians are basic rational homogeneous varieties, and the two compared quantities have canonical meanings: Plücker degree counts a generic complementary linear section, while Euler characteristic counts Bruhat cells. The theorem gives a complete all-parameter phase diagram, shows equality never occurs, isolates a unique non-projective exception, and explains the permanence of the transition by an exact growth inequality. This is a natural structural classification rather than a routine recomputation of isolated values.
